name: Receiving test carriers preserve local source closure
asks: The existing Code carrier producer and receiver must preserve every declared receiving test and its actual local module and resource dependencies; an entry-file presence check cannot establish a usable receiving carrier.

met-when.says: The original producer derives its entries from the actual package receivingTests and source declarations, using original JavaScript module/source readers; entries, roots, native resolution contexts and finite resource bounds are explicit parameters.

Before packaging, every recursively selected static or literal dynamic local module and actual local file resource is either selected by the carrier files projection or received as an explicit independently owned input. The producer does not copy foreign package source or blanket-select test directories.

Computed imports, generated fixtures, native supplier-relative imports and directory bases remain distinguished by original source evidence. A computed or unavailable dependency is not silently counted as closed; supplying original runtime/provider context remains an explicit receiving obligation.

The original final archive receiver verifies the selected local closure against actual source and archive member identities, modes and bytes; declared file names or npm output do not substitute for native archive receiving. Artifact construction does not claim tests ran or runtime activation succeeded.

Necessary implementation is generated through the existing Code and JavaScript source-generation owners from this requirement; no handwritten task scanner, fixture, test or production implementation substitutes for that chain. Existing qualified source readers and package-data writers continue the authorized declaration receiving.
